computer-use/api-reference:
Desktop control endpoints proxy authenticated commands to the agent inside the Computer.
All of them require the Computer to be `running`; a stopped or provisioning Computer returns `409 COMPUTER_NOT_RUNNING`.

Base path: `/api/v1/computers/{id}/desktop`.

> **Note: Two hosts, one contract**
>
> Full surface is on `api.miosa.ai`.
> The narrower developer host `sandboxes.miosa.ai` exposes the read and common-action endpoints only: screenshot, screenshot/region, click, type, key, scroll, drag, double-click, wait, windows, cursor, screen-size, accessibility-tree, window/focus, launch, and window-state.
> The low-level endpoints listed below - hotkey, key-down/key-up, mouse-down/mouse-up, move, clipboard, wallpaper, environment, and per-window geometry - are on `api.miosa.ai`.

## Observation

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/screenshot` | Full desktop as PNG (`Content-Type: image/png`) |
| `POST` | `/screenshot/region` | Rectangular region as PNG; body `{ x, y, width, height }` |
| `GET` | `/windows` | Open windows: `id`, `title`, `class`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `focused` |
| `GET` | `/cursor` | Cursor position `{ x, y }` in screen pixels |
| `GET` | `/screen-size` | Display resolution `{ width, height }` |
| `GET` | `/environment` | Desktop environment name and version (for example `xfce4`) |
| `GET` | `/accessibility-tree` | AT-SPI element tree as nested JSON |
| `GET` | `/window-state` | Screenshot **and** accessibility tree in one round trip |

### `GET /desktop/window-state`

Runs the screenshot and the accessibility tree in parallel and returns them together from the same moment, so an agent pays one round trip instead of two.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "screenshot": {
      "content_type": "image/png",
      "encoding": "base64",
      "bytes": 214733,
      "data": "iVBORw0KGgo..."
    },
    "accessibility_tree": { "role": "frame", "name": "Firefox", "children": [ ] },
    "captured_at": "2026-10-10T12:00:00.000000Z"
  }
}
```

A part that fails does not fail the request: it is `null` and named under an `errors` object, so the caller can still use the other half.
Only when both parts fail is the request a `502 AGENT_UNAVAILABLE`.

## Mouse

| Method | Path | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/click` | `x`, `y`, `button` (`left`\|`right`\|`middle`, default `left`) |
| `POST` | `/double-click` | `x`, `y` |
| `POST` | `/move` | `x`, `y` (move the pointer, no click) |
| `POST` | `/drag` | `from_x`, `from_y`, `to_x`, `to_y` |
| `POST` | `/mouse-down` | `x`, `y`, `button` (default `left`) |
| `POST` | `/mouse-up` | `x`, `y`, `button` (default `left`) |
| `POST` | `/scroll` | `x`, `y`, `direction` (`up`\|`down`\|`left`\|`right`), `clicks` |

> **Caution: mouse-down / mouse-up naming gap**
>
> The public endpoints are `/desktop/mouse-down` and `/desktop/mouse-up`.
> Inside the Computer they map to the lower-level actions named `mouse-press` and `mouse-release`.
> The names differ between the public contract and the on-machine action; the pair-and-release behavior is the same.
> For a one-shot click, use `POST /desktop/click` - do not assume the request field is named `press`.

`mouse-down` / `mouse-up` hold and release a button with no click between them, so you can move the pointer mid-drag (`move` then `mouse-up`) or implement a long press.

## Keyboard

| Method | Path | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/type` | `text`, optional `delay` (ms between keys) |
| `POST` | `/key` | `key` - a single key or a `+` chord, for example `Return` or `ctrl+a` |
| `POST` | `/hotkey` | `keys` - a simultaneous combo, for example `["ctrl", "shift", "t"]` |
| `POST` | `/key-down` | `key` - press and hold |
| `POST` | `/key-up` | `key` - release |

Key names follow the X11 keysym convention: `Return`, `Tab`, `BackSpace`, `Delete`, `Home`, `End`, `Page_Up`, `Page_Down`, `Up`, `Down`, `Left`, `Right`, `F1`-`F12`, and the modifiers `super`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`.
`type` types literal text and does not interpret key names; use `key` for those.

## Clipboard, windows, and desktop

| Method | Path | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/clipboard` | Read clipboard text |
| `POST` | `/clipboard` | `text` - write clipboard text |
| `POST` | `/window/focus` | `window_id` |
| `POST` | `/launch` | `command` - launch an app, runs in the background |
| `GET` | `/window/{window_id}/size` | Read a window's `{ width, height }` |
| `GET` | `/window/{window_id}/position` | Read a window's `{ x, y }` |
| `POST` | `/window/{window_id}/resize` | `width`, `height` |
| `POST` | `/window/{window_id}/move` | `x`, `y` |
| `POST` | `/window/{window_id}/maximize` | - |
| `POST` | `/window/{window_id}/minimize` | - |
| `POST` | `/window/{window_id}/close` | - |
| `POST` | `/wallpaper` | `path` - set the background from a file inside the VM |

## Timing

| Method | Path | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/wait` | `seconds` - sleep inside the Computer, capped at 30, to let UI animations settle |

## Related endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/computers/{id}/screenshot` | Alias for the full-desktop screenshot |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/computers/{id}/urls` | Signed desktop, VNC, terminal, and entry URLs |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/computers/{id}/stream-token` | Mint a short-lived viewer stream token |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/computers/{id}/vnc-credentials` | VNC credentials for the desktop |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/computers/{id}/viewer-password` | Read the raw external viewer password |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/computers/{id}/viewer-password/rotate` | Rotate the raw external viewer password |

## Coordinates

Coordinates are screen pixels with the origin at the top-left, matching what `screen-size` and `cursor` report.
A vision model may be shown a scaled-down screenshot; map its output back to screen pixels before sending an action.

## Errors

| Status | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `409` | `COMPUTER_NOT_RUNNING` | The Computer is stopped, provisioning, or recovering |
| `502` | `AGENT_UNAVAILABLE` | The agent inside the Computer did not answer |
| `429` | - | Rate limited; honor `X-RateLimit-*` and `Retry-After` |

See also: [Desktop API](/docs/api-reference/desktop) for the field-by-field request and response shapes.
computer-use/limits:
## Latency

Desktop methods run synchronously over authenticated HTTP RPC. Typical round-trip from the MIOSA edge:

| Method type | Typical latency |
|---|---|
| Click, key, scroll, type | 30-80 ms |
| Screenshot | 100-300 ms (compression-bound) |
| Window list | 50-100 ms |
| `bash()` / `python()` | 50 ms plus command execution time |

For high-frequency loops, prefer `bash()` for multi-step operations over many individual GUI calls.
`GET /desktop/window-state` returns the screenshot and the accessibility tree together, so perception costs one round trip instead of two.

## Coordinate space

Coordinates are screen pixels with the origin at the top-left, matching what `GET /desktop/screen-size` and `GET /desktop/cursor` report.
A vision model may be shown a scaled-down screenshot; map its output back to screen pixels before sending an action.

## Screenshots

Screenshots are PNG.
A full desktop image is typically a few hundred kilobytes; regions are smaller.
Use `/desktop/screenshot/region` when only part of the screen matters, and `window-state` when you need pixels and structure at once.

## Sizing

| Size | vCPU | RAM | Disk | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `xs` | 1 | 2 GB | 10 GB | Lightweight headless tasks |
| `small` | 2 | 4 GB | 20 GB | **Default** for a single agent and basic browsing |
| `medium` | 4 | 8 GB | 40 GB | Heavier desktop apps, faster page loads |
| `large` | 8 | 16 GB | 80 GB | Multi-app, large-context workloads |
| `xl` | 16 | 32 GB | 160 GB | Intensive parallelism |

GPU support for accelerated desktop and GPU-aware workflows is plan-dependent.

## Lifecycle

create creates provisioning; provisioning goes to running on ready; running goes to stopped on stop, and back to running on start.

running goes to recovering on host maintenance; recovering goes to running on restored.

recovering goes to error on recovery fails.

running or stopped goes to deleted on delete.

Stopping a Computer pauses compute and preserves the filesystem and browser profile.
Restarting resumes from that state.
Desktop endpoints only accept requests while the Computer is `running`; otherwise they return `409 COMPUTER_NOT_RUNNING`.

## Authentication

Desktop methods require the same workspace API key as every other MIOSA resource.
Call them server-side.
For browser-side control, mint a scoped token instead of shipping the API key - see [Embedding & streaming](/docs/computers/embedding).

> **Caution: Never expose the API key**
>
> Mint stream URLs and scoped tokens on your backend.
> Send only the short-lived URL or token to the browser.

## Rate limits

Rate limits vary by key, tenant policy, and endpoint family.
Honor `X-RateLimit-*` and `Retry-After` response headers.
Individual desktop actions are fast, but a tight perceive-act loop still issues many requests; batch where the work does not need pixels.

## Errors

| Status | Code | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `409` | `COMPUTER_NOT_RUNNING` | The Computer is stopped, provisioning, or recovering |
| `502` | `AGENT_UNAVAILABLE` | The agent inside the Computer did not answer |
| `429` | - | Rate limited |
computer-use/quickstart:
Create a Computer, take a screenshot, act once, and screenshot again.
This is the loop every computer-use agent runs, whether it is headless or watched by a person.

## 1. Create and start a Computer

**Python**

```python
import miosa, os

client = miosa.Miosa(api_key=os.environ["MIOSA_API_KEY"])

computer = client.computers.create(name="agent-1", template_type="miosa-desktop", size="small")
computer.start()
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
import { Miosa } from "@miosa/sdk"

const miosa = new Miosa({ apiKey: process.env.MIOSA_API_KEY! })

const computer = await miosa.computers.create({
  name: "agent-1",
  template_type: "miosa-desktop",
  size: "small",
})
await computer.start()
```

`start()` returns once the desktop is running and accepting actions.
Computer state is `provisioning`, `running`, `stopped`, `recovering`, `error`, or `deleted`.

## 2. The first loop

Capture, decide, act once, capture again.
Do not issue several blind actions in a row.

**Python**

```python
png = computer.screenshot()

# Decide from the screenshot, or read the accessibility tree for structured elements.
tree = computer.get_accessibility_tree()

computer.left_click(640, 480)
after = computer.screenshot()   # verify the UI changed
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
const png = await computer.screenshot()

const tree = await computer.desktop.accessibilityTree()

await computer.leftClick(640, 480)
const after = await computer.screenshot()
```

**REST**

```bash
curl https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/computers/$CID/desktop/screenshot \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" --output before.png

curl -X POST https://api.miosa.ai/api/v1/computers/$CID/desktop/click \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MIOSA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"x": 640, "y": 480, "button": "left"}'
```

Coordinates are screen pixels with the origin at the top-left.
Read the current resolution with `get_screen_size()` if you need to scale a model's output.

> **Tip: One action, one observation**
>
> A loop that screenshots after every action is slower per step but far more reliable than a batch of guessed actions.
> For multi-step shell work that does not need pixels, prefer `bash()` over a long chain of GUI calls.

## 3. Watch it live

The same running desktop can be shown to a browser.
On the platform, open the Computer and use the desktop button.
In your own app, mint a short-lived stream URL on your backend and embed it.

**Python**

```python
urls = computer.urls()
print(urls["desktop_url"])   # pass this to your frontend, never your API key
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
const urls = await computer.urls()
// <iframe src={urls.desktop_url} sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts" />
```

See [Embedding & streaming](/docs/computers/embedding) for the token flow, iframe policy, and expiry handling.

## 4. A full agent loop

```python
import anthropic, os
from miosa import Miosa

miosa_client  = Miosa(api_key=os.environ["MIOSA_API_KEY"])
claude_client = anthropic.Anthropic()

computer = miosa_client.computers.create(name="browser-agent", template_type="miosa-desktop", size="small")
computer.start()
computer.launch("firefox")

for _ in range(10):
    b64 = computer.screenshot_base64()

    response = claude_client.messages.create(
        model="claude-opus-4-5",
        max_tokens=1024,
        messages=[{
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png", "data": b64}},
                {"type": "text", "text": "Navigate to miosa.ai and screenshot the homepage."},
            ],
        }],
    )

    # Parse an action from the model output, then act once.
    text = response.content[0].text
    if "left_click" in text:
        computer.left_click(500, 500)
    elif "type" in text:
        computer.type("https://miosa.ai\n")

computer.stop()
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant AG as Agent
    participant CM as Computer

    AG->>CM: screenshot_base64()
    CM-->>AG: PNG (base64)
    AG->>AG: reason about the next action
    AG->>CM: left_click(x, y)
    AG->>CM: type(text)
    AG->>CM: screenshot_base64()
    AG->>AG: task complete?
```

computer-use/sdk-examples:
The Python and TypeScript SDKs expose the same desktop contract.
In TypeScript the desktop methods also live on `computer.desktop`.
Method names are case-sensitive.

## Method reference

| Group | Python | TypeScript | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Screen** | `screenshot()` | `screenshot()` | Full desktop as PNG bytes |
| | `screenshot_base64()` | `screenshotBase64()` | Same, base64, ready for a vision model |
| | `screenshot_region(x, y, w, h)` | `screenshotRegion(x, y, w, h)` | Region as PNG bytes |
| **Click** | `click(x, y, button="left")` | `click(x, y, button)` | Click at pixels; button `left`\|`right`\|`middle` |
| | `left_click(x, y)` | `leftClick(x, y)` | Left-button click |
| | `right_click(x, y)` | `rightClick(x, y)` | Right-button click |
| | - | `middleClick(x, y)` | Middle-button click |
| | `double_click(x, y)` | `doubleClick(x, y)` | Double-click |
| **Mouse** | `move_cursor(x, y)` | `moveMouse(x, y)` | Move the pointer without clicking |
| | `mouse_down(x, y, button="left")` | `mouseDown(x, y, button)` | Press and hold a button |
| | `mouse_up(x, y, button="left")` | `mouseUp(x, y, button)` | Release a held button |
| | `drag(from_x, from_y, to_x, to_y)` | `drag(fromX, fromY, toX, toY)` | Click-drag between two points |
| **Keyboard** | `type(text)` | `type(text)` | Type literal text at the focus |
| | `key(key)` | `key(key)` | Press one key or a `+` chord |
| | `hotkey(*keys)` | `hotkey(...keys)` | Simultaneous combo |
| | `key_down(key)` / `key_up(key)` | `keyDown(key)` / `keyUp(key)` | Hold or release a key |
| **Scroll** | `scroll(direction, clicks)` | `scroll(direction, clicks)` | Scroll `up`\|`down`\|`left`\|`right` by N notches |
| | `scroll_up/down/left/right(clicks)` | - | Convenience scrolls |
| **Clipboard** | `get_clipboard()` / `set_clipboard(text)` | `getClipboard()` / `setClipboard(text)` | Read or write clipboard text |
| **Screen info** | `get_screen_size()` | `screenSize()` | Resolution `{ width, height }` |
| | `get_cursor_position()` | `cursor()` | Cursor `{ x, y }` in screen pixels |
| **Windows** | `windows()` | `windows()` | List open windows |
| | `launch(app)` | `launch(appName)` | Open an installed app |
| | `focus_window(id)` | `focusWindow(id)` | Bring a window to the front |
| | `get_window_size(id)` / `set_window_size(id, w, h)` | `windowSize(id)` / `resizeWindow(id, w, h)` | Read or set window size |
| | `get_window_position(id)` / `set_window_position(id, x, y)` | `windowPosition(id)` / `moveWindow(id, x, y)` | Read or set window position |
| | `maximize_window(id)` / `minimize_window(id)` / `close_window(id)` | `maximizeWindow(id)` / `minimizeWindow(id)` / `closeWindow(id)` | Change window state |
| **Environment** | `get_desktop_environment()` | `environment()` | DE name and version |
| | `set_wallpaper(path)` | `setWallpaper(path)` | Set the background from a VM file |
| | `get_accessibility_tree()` | `accessibilityTree()` | AT-SPI element tree |
| **Shell and files** | `bash(cmd)` / `python(code)` | `bash(cmd)` / `python(code)` | Run inside the VM |
| | `write_file(path, content)` / `read_file(path)` | `writeFile(path, content)` / `readFile(path)` | Read or write a VM file |

## First loop

**Python**

```python
png = computer.screenshot()

# Decide from the image, or read the accessibility tree for structured elements.
tree = computer.get_accessibility_tree()

computer.left_click(500, 500)
after = computer.screenshot()
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
const png = await computer.screenshot()
const tree = await computer.desktop.accessibilityTree()

await computer.leftClick(500, 500)
const after = await computer.screenshot()
```

## Feed a screenshot to a vision model

`Screenshot_base64` returns a string you can pass straight through as image data.

```python
b64 = computer.screenshot_base64()

import anthropic
client = anthropic.Anthropic()
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-4-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png", "data": b64}},
            {"type": "text", "text": "What is on screen, and where should I click?"},
        ],
    }],
)
```

## Keyboard and mouse

**Python**

```python
computer.type("hello, world")     # literal text
computer.key("Return")            # one key
computer.key("ctrl+a")            # a chord
computer.hotkey("ctrl", "shift", "t")

computer.key_down("shift")
computer.left_click(800, 200)     # shift-click to extend a selection
computer.key_up("shift")

computer.mouse_down(200, 200)
computer.move_cursor(400, 400)    # move while held
computer.mouse_up(400, 400)
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
await computer.type("hello, world")
await computer.key("Return")
await computer.desktop.hotkey("ctrl", "shift", "t")

await computer.desktop.keyDown("shift")
await computer.leftClick(800, 200)
await computer.desktop.keyUp("shift")

await computer.desktop.mouseDown(200, 200)
await computer.desktop.moveMouse(400, 400)
await computer.desktop.mouseUp(400, 400)
```

## Clipboard, scroll, and windows

**Python**

```python
computer.set_clipboard("text to paste")
computer.hotkey("ctrl", "v")

computer.scroll("down", clicks=3)
computer.scroll_up(clicks=5)

w = computer.windows()[0]
computer.focus_window(w["id"])
computer.set_window_size(w["id"], 1280, 800)
computer.set_window_position(w["id"], 100, 50)
computer.maximize_window(w["id"])
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
await computer.desktop.setClipboard("text to paste")
await computer.desktop.hotkey("ctrl", "v")

await computer.scroll("down", 3)

const w = (await computer.windows())[0]
await computer.focusWindow(w.id)
await computer.desktop.resizeWindow(w.id, 1280, 800)
await computer.desktop.moveWindow(w.id, 100, 50)
await computer.desktop.maximizeWindow(w.id)
```

## Shell, Python, and files

These run inside the VM with no GUI interaction and are usually the fastest way to do multi-step work.

```python
print(computer.bash("ls /workspace/Desktop"))
print(computer.python("print(1 + 1)"))

computer.write_file("/workspace/script.py", "print('hello')")
computer.bash("python3 /workspace/script.py")
print(computer.read_file("/workspace/.bashrc"))
```

## CLI

```bash
miosa api GET "/computers/$COMPUTER_ID/desktop/screenshot" > before.png
miosa api GET "/computers/$COMPUTER_ID/desktop/accessibility-tree"
miosa api POST "/computers/$COMPUTER_ID/desktop/click" -d '{"x": 500, "y": 500}'
miosa api GET "/computers/$COMPUTER_ID/desktop/screenshot" > after.png
```

computer-use/vs-browser-use:
Both drive a real browser. They differ in how much machine you rent.

> **Note: The rule**
>
> If the task is a web page an agent or a person should watch, use [Browser use](/docs/browser-use) - it runs in any sandbox and bills as ordinary sandbox usage.
> If the task needs a full desktop, other apps, or takeover of the whole screen, use [Computer use](/docs/computer-use).

| | Browser use | Computer use |
|---|---|---|
| What runs | A live browser inside a sandbox | A full Linux desktop on a Computer |
| Where | Any sandbox, any template | A Computer you create and start |
| Setup | On by default; nothing to choose at create time | Create a Computer, then start it |
| Live viewer | On the Sandbox page: take control, view-only share links, full screen | A streamable desktop, embeddable with a short-lived URL |
| Agent access | Over CDP - Playwright, Puppeteer | Screenshot and control APIs: mouse, keyboard, windows, accessibility |
| Human takeover | The browser view | The whole desktop |
| Other apps | No - browser only | Yes - any installed Linux app |
| Persistence | Survives pause and resume | Survives stop and start |
| Billing | Plain sandbox usage | Computer compute while running |
| Best for | Web automation, scraping, logged-in browser work that should be watched | GUI apps, desktop workflows, screenshot QA, full human handoff |

## Pick browser use when

- The task lives entirely on web pages.
- You want the cheapest isolated environment: a sandbox you already use for code.
- A person should be able to watch, take control, or share a view-only link.
- Playwright or Puppeteer is your driver.

## Pick computer use when

- The task needs desktop apps, file pickers, extensions, or multiple windows.
- The agent works from pixels and the accessibility tree across the whole screen.
- A human must take over the exact machine an agent was using.
- You need a durable desktop that keeps its browser profile and installed tools across restarts.

## Next

- [Browser use](/docs/browser-use) - start a live browser in any sandbox.
- [Computer use](/docs/computer-use) - the desktop perception-action loop.
